thread:
mina: Quick heads-up from today's onboarding lab: multiple quickstart snippets are out of sync again.
mina: Noticed three different env var names across docs/examples: REDWOOD_TOKEN, REDWOOD_API, and REDWOOD_API_KEY. New hires copied the Docker devcontainer snippet and set REDWOOD_TOKEN and got confused.
ethan: Ugh. Which files are hitting this?
mina: Quick list: README.md quickstart curl, docs/examples/js/quickstart.js, examples/devcontainer/Dockerfile.env, and the python snippet in docs/python/quickstart.md.
mina: Also the README shows a bash-only multiline curl without calling out PowerShell, and our Docker devcontainer example has an .env file using REDWOOD_TOKEN so the sample app fails when people follow the container flow.
cleo: Thanks for catching. We should: (1) pick one canonical env var name and update everything (vote for REDWOOD_API_KEY), (2) update README to include single-line curl + PowerShell Invoke-RestMethod, (3) fix the devcontainer .env to use the canonical name, and (4) add a tiny non-network smoke test in docs CI to run a local node script that validates env var usage.
vik: For the TS/JS import style, can we add both import styles and a short note about esModuleInterop? We keep seeing `import Redwood from` in the example app which breaks stricter tsconfigs.
ethan: Agreed on all points. I'll open a PR to normalize env var to REDWOOD_API_KEY across docs, examples, and the devcontainer. I'll also add docs/examples/quickstart-smoke.js which only checks process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY and exits 1 if not set, so CI can catch copy/paste drift.
mina: Can we also add a docs lint rule (simple grep) that fails if README or examples reference REDWOOD_TOKEN or REDWOOD_API? That will be a cheap guardrail.
ethan: Yep. I'll add a grep-based check in the docs CI step (docs:lint) that searches for the deprecated names.
doc-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/912  normalizes env var to REDWOOD_API_KEY, updates curl/PowerShell examples, fixes devcontainer .env, adds quickstart-smoke.js, and adds a docs grep lint job.
cleo: Nice. One extra ask: can we also add a short note in the onboarding checklist and the new-hire lab README about how to set env vars in mac/linux/windows and how to test the devcontainer? New hires kept assuming the container injected secrets automatically.
vik: Good catch. I'll update the onboarding lab and add a quick note: "Set REDWOOD_API_KEY in your host or devcontainer .env; the devcontainer does not auto-populate secrets."
mina: Thanks! Once the PR merges I'll re-run the onboarding lab and report back if anything else pops up. :thumbsup:
